rules.statement: A status type interrupt must drive a wired level-triggered interrupt directly from the hardware input signal, qualified only by INTR_ENABLE, staying asserted while the input is asserted.
The wired status interrupt must not deassert until the root cause of the hardware input signal is addressed by software intervention.
Software cannot acknowledge a status type interrupt through INTR_STATE, which is read-only (ro) in this context.
The generic component prim_intr_hw can generate the correct status interrupt hardware when parameterized with .IntrT("Status").

rules.condition: SW cannot address the root cause or wishes to defer handling
rules.statement: Software should mask the interrupt, at the peripheral or further up the tree such as the PLIC.
Masking at the peripheral can be achieved by clearing the corresponding bit in INTR_ENABLE.
The block diagram shows one possible hardware implementation of interrupt foo; other implementations are permitted.
The event must set the associated bit in INTR_STATE to 1.

rules.condition: Write of 1 to the foo bit of INTR_TEST
rules.statement: A write of 1 to the associated foo bit of INTR_TEST can set the corresponding INTR_STATE bit.
The outgoing interrupt intr_foo_o must be the INTR_STATE output ANDed with INTR_ENABLE.

rules.condition: Software writes 1 to the INTR_STATE bit
rules.statement: A write of 1 to an INTR_STATE bit clears the latched value, but INTR_STATE returns to true if the event is still active.
Hardware must not clear the latched interrupt state; only software can clear it.
Each peripheral can send zero or more alerts, each a distinguishable security threat.
Each alert originates in an internal event and must be specially handled within the peripheral and then within the alert handler module.
A recoverable alert must be one-time triggered: the alert sender transmits a single alert event when the error condition is asserted.
A fatal alert must be continuously transmitted by the alert sender until the system is reset.

rules.condition: Fatal alert and local countermeasures exist
rules.statement: Fatal alerts should also trigger local security countermeasures.
Error conditions should use the recommended alert type listed in the table; the regular IRQ column entries marked (x) are optional.
A peripheral may optionally send a regular IRQ for any alert event, if needed by the programming model.
Alerts shall be given a meaningful name indicative of their cause.
Recoverable alerts must be prefixed with recov_ and fatal alerts must be prefixed with fatal_.

rules.condition: Many diverse sources bundled into one alert event
rules.statement: Alert names may default to just recov and/or fatal, implying no more than one alert of that type is exposed.
Every peripheral has a write-only (wo) ALERT_TEST register for software to test alert reporting in the alert handler.
Every alert has one field bit in ALERT_TEST, connected to the test input of the corresponding prim_alert_sender.
Internal events are sent active-high to the prim_alert_sender within the peripheral.
One prim_alert_sender must be instantiated per distinct alert event, with IsFatal set to 1 for fatal alerts so the alert is latched until reset.
The peripheral maintainer determines distinct alert events; multiple sources can be bundled depending on the required distinction.
Each peripheral should bundle alert sources into one or two distinct alerts, for example one fatal and one recoverable.

rules.condition: Comportable IP with multiple bundled alerts
rules.statement: The IP should expose a cause register for disambiguation.
Cause registers for recoverable alerts must be clearable by SW or automatically cleared by HW.
Cause registers for fatal alerts must not be clearable in any way and must be read-only.
The prim_alert_sender converts the event into a differentially encoded signal pair routed to the hardware alert handler.
The alert handler is generated with enough alert ports for each alert declared in the included peripheral configuration files.
